comments.text_zh: 给不知道的人说一下，这是斯坦福教授 Robert Sapolsky 的一本书：[LINK] 这本书讲的是压力以及 glucocorticoids 对身体的影响。动物在“野外”使用的那套化学压力反应，其实和我们担心失业、赶不完学校论文、应付贫困等时的压力反应是同一套。这能部分解释为什么现代人会有这么多慢性病，而这些病在其他动物身上很少见（甚至在非工业社会的考古/人类学证据里也很少见，不过他在书里没怎么往这个方向展开）。我也强烈推荐 Sapolsky 在斯坦福讲授、后来发布到 YouTube 上的“人类行为生物学”课程：[VIDEO]
comments.text: for anyone unaware, this is a book by Stanford professor Robert Sapolsky: [LINK] The book is about stress and the impact of glucocorticoids on the body. The chemical stress response used in "the wild" by animals is actually the same as the stress response we have when worrying about losing our job, not being able to complete a paper for school, dealing with poverty, etc. It's a partial explanation for why modern humans have so many chronic diseases that are rarely seen in other animals (or even archeological/anthropological evidence of non-industrial societies but he doesn't really go there much in the book) I also highly recommend Sapolsky's Human Behavior Biology course which he taught for Stanford but published on YouTube: [VIDEO]

comments.text: Anyone who wants to look at heritability numbers should make sure to watch these lectures first. Heritability is often a misleading stat, because it has an unintuitive definition. [LINK] [LINK] Full Lectures: [VIDEO] An example of how non-intuitive heritability is: whether a person wears earrings or not would be a heritable trait if we're looking at mid-20th century America, because the variability is entirely explained by whether you're male or female. Heritability is unable to identify whether a trait is caused by genetics, only whether the variation correlates with genetics.

They joined the same flock recently and after a large fight over dominance the young male acquired injuries and died. comments.text_zh: 如果你不把基督教看成一个界限清晰的类别，而是把它看成更广泛的宗教模式家族中的一团实践、信仰和制度，那就更妙了。Mircea Eliade 追问基督教如何重新诠释神圣历史、神话、救赎。基督教如何处理那些比它自身更古老的母题，比如天堂、重生、献祭？在《A History of Religious Ideas》[0] 中，他论述了基督教的出现与发展，包括犹太教、早期基督教、诺斯替主义、晚期古代、中世纪宗教形态，以及它如何与其他传统互动。我觉得这本书很好地补充了基督教的地理传播这一视角，同时也说清了究竟是哪些宗教象征的转变，让基督教在如此不同的语境中仍可被辨认出来。还有《Darwin's Cathedral》[1]，它把宗教作为一种群体组织系统来分析，重点讲加尔文主义。我没细读，但看起来挺相关。它是 Robert Sapolsky 在“人类行为生物学导论”系列讲座里推荐的 [2]。[0] A History of Religious Ideas - Mircea Eliade [1] Darwin's Cathedral - David Sloan Wilson [2] [VIDEO]
comments.text: It's even more amazing when you think about Christianity not as a clear category, but as a cloud of practices, beliefs and institutions in a broader family of religious patterns. Mircea Eliade asks how Christianity reinterpreted sacred history, myth, salvation. What does Christianity do with motifs older than itself, such as paradise, rebirth, sacrifice? In A History of Religious Ideas [0], he treats the emergence and development of Christianity, including Judaism, early Christianity, Gnosticism, late antiquity, medieval religious forms and also how it interacted with other traditions. I think it complements quite nicely the geographical spread of Christianity by also clarifying what kind of transformations of religious symbols make it recognisable as Christianity across such different contexts. There's also "Darwin's Cathedral" [1] that analyses religion as group-organizing system, with a focus on Calvinism. Didn't go through it, but seems relevant. It was recommended by Robert Sapolsky in his Introduction to Human Behavioral Biology lecture series [2].
